## Solution

**Setup.** The silk scarf is a square of side $100\text{ mm} = 10\text{ cm}$, so its total area is
$$10 \times 10 = 100\text{ cm}^2.$$

**Each removed triangle.** From a corner, the designer measures $40\text{ mm}$ along one edge and $20\text{ mm}$ along the adjacent edge, then cuts along the straight line connecting these two points. This removes a right triangle with legs $40\text{ mm}$ and $20\text{ mm}$ (the two edges meeting at the corner form a right angle). Its area is
$$\tfrac{1}{2}\times 40\times 20 = 400\text{ mm}^2 = 4\text{ cm}^2.$$

**Two identical cuts.** The two cuts are made at *opposite* corners. Since each triangle extends at most $40\text{ mm}$ along an edge of the $100\text{ mm}$ square, and the two corners are opposite, the two triangles are far apart and do not overlap. (The closest approach along any edge is $100 - 40 - 20 = 40\text{ mm} > 0$, and even along the diagonal the triangles are well separated.) Thus the total removed area is simply
$$2 \times 4 = 8\text{ cm}^2.$$

**Remaining area.**
$$100 - 8 = 92\text{ cm}^2.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
